name: H5N1 bird flu
value: Cattle-linked US cases; no human spread
summary: Recent US H5N1 cases in Yakima County were all linked to infected cattle; ECDC finds no sustained human spread
state: ECDC's update of 9 Nov counts 74 US human H5 cases since April 2024 to 5 Nov, plus the recent Yakima County, Washington, cases linked to infected dairy cattle, one of which was fatal; it reports no new case after 3 Nov and no sustained human-to-human transmission (ECDC). UKHSA's report published 12 Nov notes poultry-linked H9N2 cases in China, also without sustained human spread. These remain animal-to-human cases, so the level stays Normal.
for_you: The general public risk is rated low. People working with poultry or dairy cattle can follow UKHSA and NHS guidance on avoiding contact with sick or dead birds and animals.
rubric_hit: Sporadic animal-to-human cases only; no human cluster or sustained human spread (ECDC, 9 Nov) = Normal

sources.title: ECDC — Avian influenza A(H5N1) human cases, United States 2024–2026 (update 9 Nov)

why: H5N1 is the flu strain scientists most fear could become a pandemic; it has spread to mammals and dairy cattle.
drivers: Human cases, mammal-to-mammal spread, mutations, surveillance.

rubric.watch: Human clusters under investigation, rising human cases, or new mammalian species spread.
